properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 11 at 3:01PM EDT until October 12 at 2:00AM EDT by NWS Baltimore MD/Washington DC
properties.description:
After a widespread 1.50 to 2.50 inches of rainfall, expect a bit of
a lull this afternoon before another round of more concentrated
shower activity forms near the area low of pressure associated with
Isaias. Some flooding concerns will accompany this feature given
earlier soaking rains.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of central, northern, and northwest Virginia,
including the following areas, in central Virginia, Albemarle,
Central Virginia Blue Ridge, Greene, Nelson and Orange. In northern
Virginia, Culpeper, Northern Fauquier and Southern Fauquier. In
northwest Virginia, Madison, Northern Virginia Blue Ridge and
Rappahannock.

* WHEN...Until 2 AM EDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Low-water crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Despite a lull in the activity this afternoon, another round of
moderate to heavy showers are expected near the low pressure
attached to the remnants of Isaias. Locally intense rainfall
could lead to flooding concerns, especially in areas that saw the
highest rainfall amounts.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 11 at 11:08AM MST until October 12 at 5:00AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...western Coconino, northern Gila, far southern Navajo, and
Yavapai counties.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Flash flooding will be possible in creeks, normally dry
washes, swimming holes, and over recently burned areas. Raging
killer currents will be possible in side canyons and narrow slot
canyons. Low-water crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Numerous showers and thunderstorms are expected to continue
across the area through tonight. With tropical moisture in place
from the remnants of Tropical Storm Rachel, periods of embedded
heavy rainfall will be possible this afternoon which could lead
to flash flooding. Additionally, the extended period of rain
could lead to elevated flow in creeks, normally dry washes, and
rivers.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Have a way to receive Flash Flood Warnings and be prepared to take
action should warnings be issued.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 11 at 6:42AM MDT until October 12 at 6:00PM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of Utah, including the following areas, Castle
Country, Central Mountains, Eastern Juab/Millard Counties, San
Rafael Swell, Sanpete Valley, Sevier Valley, Wasatch Plateau/Book
Cliffs, Bryce Canyon Country, Capitol Reef National Park and
Vicinity, Glen Canyon Recreation Area/Lake Powell, South Central
Utah, Southern Mountains, Upper Sevier River Valleys, Western
Canyonlands, Lower Washington County, Southwest Utah and Zion
National Park. This also includes recent burn scars such as
Forsyth, Cottonwood, Silver King, France Canyon, and Monroe Canyon.

* WHEN...Through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, dry washes, slot canyons, and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations such as slickrock areas and recent burn
scars. Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may
occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Anomalously high moisture from the remnants of Tropical Storm
Rachel will continue to impact the region. While this is expected
to be a long duration rainfall event, scattered instances of
heavier rainfall rates are expected with stronger storms yielding
flash flooding concerns given saturated soils and prior burn
scars.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 11 at 6:42AM MDT until October 12 at 6:00PM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of Utah, including the following areas, Western
Millard and Juab Counties, Bear Lake and Bear River Valley, Cache
Valley/Utah Portion, Eastern Box Elder County, Great Salt Lake
Desert and Mountains, Northern Wasatch Front, Salt Lake Valley,
Tooele and Rush Valleys, Utah Valley, Wasatch Back, Wasatch
Mountains I-80 North, Wasatch Mountains South of I-80, Western
Uinta Basin and Western Uinta Mountains. This includes recent burn
scars such as Rocky Canyon.

* WHEN...Through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and recent burn scars. Flooding may occur in poor
drainage and urban areas. Extensive street flooding and flooding of
creeks and rivers are possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Moisture associated with the remnants of Tropical Storm Rachel
will continue to spread into northern Utah producing a prolonged
rainfall event. In particular, moisture interacting with a
frontal boundary across far northern Utah may yield locally
heavier rainfall totals compared to other locations. As a result,
areal flooding is possible across northern Utah.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 11 at 1:08AM PDT until October 12 at 5:00AM PDT by NWS Elko NV
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall and debris flows
are possible.

* WHERE...Portions of eastern, northeast, and south central Nevada,
including the following areas, in eastern Nevada, White Pine. In
northeast Nevada, the Ruby Mountains and East Humboldt Range in
Elko, South Central Elko and Southeastern Elko. In south central
Nevada, Northeastern Nye and Northwestern Nye.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams,
and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. In addition, flash
flooding is possible over recently burned areas like the former
Ward Fire, Kearny Fire, Oxley Fire, Secret Pass Fire, Starr Valley
Fire, Jones Fire, and Egberts Fire. Other burn scar locations in
the watch area could also be affected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Deep moisture from decaying Hurricane Rachel is expected to move
northward, crossing into portions of east-central and eastern
Nevada late tonight through roughly Monday. This significant
moisture will interact with upper level low pressure to bring
widespread showers with isolated thunderstorms to the watch area.
Moderate to locally heavy rain will cause excessive runoff and
may result in rock, mud, and debris flows in and near former fire
burned areas, steep terrain, and poorly drained urban areas.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
